site.title: Forteana
site.description: Practical guides on Forteana, organized for fast browsing and comparison.

pages.title: Forteana
pages.summary: Forteana is the loose field of stories, reports and arguments that cluster around strange events which seem to fall between accepted categories: fish or frogs said to fall from the sky, ghostly figures, cryptids, unusual aerial sightings, uncanny coincidences, miraculous claims, and other anomalies that are reported often enough to be culturally...

pages.title: Animal Falls
pages.summary: Reports of raining fish and frogs show how rare natural events can become lasting mysteries.

pages.title: Checklist
pages.summary: A strong animal-fall investigation separates what witnesses saw from what moved the animals there, then tests weather, species, location, and alternatives.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index

pages.title: Marksville
pages.summary: The Marksville case remains memorable because it has named reporting and a clear date, yet still shows why older animal falls rarely settle mechanisms.

pages.title: Not Falling

pages.title: One Species
pages.summary: A fall made mostly of one species raises a harder question than scattered pond debris because real water bodies contain messy mixtures of life.

pages.title: Texarkana Fish

pages.title: Waterspouts

pages.title: Anomalistics

pages.title: Psychology

pages.title: Taos Hum
pages.summary: The Taos Hum became the model modern hum mystery because sincere reports met serious study without a clear shared source.

pages.title: Windsor
pages.summary: The Windsor Hum turned a local noise complaint into a cross-border dispute about evidence, authority, and responsibility.

pages.title: Weather
pages.summary: Storms, waterspouts, whirlwinds, and heavy rain can make rare events look supernatural.

pages.title: Debris Clues
pages.summary: Leaves, mud, weed and silt can make an animal-fall report more plausible by pointing to a nearby source and transport path.

pages.title: Bird Drops
pages.summary: Some fish falls may come from startled birds dropping or regurgitating fish rather than from a waterspout.

pages.title: Frog Rains
pages.summary: Many frog rains may begin when wet weather drives hidden amphibians onto roads, lawns and playing fields at once.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Weather.

pages.title: Dust Rain
pages.summary: Red or dirty rain can look supernatural when desert dust mixes with falling rain and leaves coloured residue behind.

pages.title: Worm Falls
pages.summary: Worms can suddenly cover pavements after rain, creating a vivid but misleading impression that they came down with the storm.

pages.title: Yoro Fish
pages.summary: The Yoro fish rain is harder to explain as a simple sea-to-town fall, making local flooding and hidden waterways central to the puzzle.

pages.title: Witnesses
pages.summary: Witness accounts are vital to Forteana, but memory, expectation, fear, and retelling can change a case.

pages.title: Sincerity
pages.summary: Sincerity can make a report worth hearing, but it does not turn memory into a replayable recording.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Witnesses.

pages.title: London Monster
pages.summary: The 1790 London Monster panic shows how fear, publicity, and accusation can make testimony harder to separate from social contagion.

pages.title: Observation
pages.summary: The most useful testimony often begins by stripping dramatic labels away from what was actually seen, heard, or felt.

pages.title: UAP Files
pages.summary: GEIPAN and Project Blue Book show why testimony becomes more useful when reports are sorted, checked, and limited by evidence quality.

pages.title: Rumor Waves
pages.summary: Once a strange story spreads, later witnesses may describe not only what happened but what the rumor taught them to notice.

pages.title: Sleep Visitors
pages.summary: Night-visitor reports can feel utterly real while sharing features with known sleep paralysis experiences.
